content.text:
The architectural passage surveys medieval Italian Romanesque and Gothic styles, praising Southern Italy’s ornate detail while criticizing its weak planning, small windows, limited vaulting, and dependence on painting. It discusses churches and monuments at Naples, Pisa, Siena, Florence, Milan, Bari, and elsewhere.

The accompanying animal tales follow Chop-Chin, who enters the Golden Dragon’s temple, drugs the priests, steals the idol, and confronts the Emperor. Mice leave their cellar, enter the kitchen and cupboard, and eat pie. Forest friends attend a woodmouse wedding, help a hermit in his cave, defend the cottage from a robber, and later welcome a hawk. Eileen meets a Green Man in the forest, receives a disastrous jewel-speaking gift, is taken to Dr. O’Shaughnessy’s house, escapes back to the forest, and has the spell removed. The animals eventually depart the cottage for the forest in spring.
